statement: ▶ Problem 12. Is it true that u0 (n) = u1 (n)?
context: In this paper we proved that a 1-planar unit distance graph on n vertices can have at most √ u1 (n) ≤ 3n − 4 n/10 edges. However, the best known lower bound construction for u1 (n) is the same as for u0 (n). ▶ Problem 12. Is it true that u0 (n) = u1 (n)? For k = 2 there is aq slightly better construction by Dániel Simon (personal communication, 192 2023) of roughly 3n − 23 n edges and for k = 3 there is an easy construction (a piece of a √ unit triangular grid and its shifted copy by a unit vector) with 3.5n − c n edges. For a larger k our lower and upper bounds for uk (n) are very far from each other. ▶ Problem 13. Determine the maximum number of edges of a k-planar unit distance graph.

statement: ▶ Problem 14. Are there 5-regular 1-planar unit distance graphs?
context: There are r-regular matchstick graphs for r ≤ 4 [9, 21] and there are no r-regular matchstick graphs for r ≥ 5 [4, 11]. It follows from Theorem 1 that there are no r-regular 1-planar unit distance graphs for r ≥ 6. ▶ Problem 14. Are there 5-regular 1-planar unit distance graphs?
